# Unticking Content-sized rows jumps to other rows instead of keeping the ones in view

## Context

Found in team:engine 13.3 release testing, 2026-10-20, with headless Chrome against the dev server on `dev` a77926bae8. In `examples/grid/issues`, wheel to mid-list (#19515–#19477 in view) and untick *Content-sized rows*. The view then shows #19220–#19177, none of the issues that were in view. A read-only sweep saw the same in `examples/grid/contentSizedRows`: row 5000 jumps to rows 9976–10000, row 1000 to 2619, row 2500 to 6323. Ticking the box back on keeps the place. Only switching off loses it.

13.3's notes promise the opposite. "What you can try", step 2: "Untick *Content-sized rows* to see the same issues at a fixed height."

## The Problem

Switching from content-sized to fixed rows keeps the scroll's pixel offset, not the rows the reader was looking at. Fixed rows are shorter than content-sized ones, so the same offset lands much further down the list.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/View.mjs#afterSetContentSizedRows`: switching off destroys `rowGeometry` and calls `refreshRowGeometry(true)`, which then runs `me.syncBodies(me.scrollTop, force)` with the old pixel offset.
- With a `rowGeometry`, a row's offset is measured. Without one, it is `index × rowHeight`.
- The 13.3 notes' *Keeping your place while heights arrive* already holds the first visible record while heights change (`GridRowScrollPinning`). The geometry switch bypasses it.
- Design authority: the notes' "What you can try" step 2, and the content-sized rows chapter's place-keeping promise.

## The Fix

Before the geometry changes, take the first visible row and how far into it the viewport starts. After the change, scroll so that the same row sits at the same point in the viewport, in either direction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: in `examples/grid/issues`, scrolled mid-list, unticking *Content-sized rows* keeps the first visible issue in view, and ticking it again keeps it too.
- [ ] AC-2: a browser e2e reproduces AC-1, fails on `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [ ] AC-3: at the top of the list, both directions stay at the top.

## Out of Scope

- Keeping the exact pixel position inside the row when the row's height changes.

## Related

- #19712 (the 13.3 notes). If this misses the cut, step 2 of "What you can try" needs rewording.

- 2026-10-20T12:15:35Z @tobiu referenced in commit `58bdbcd` - "fix(grid): switching row modes keeps the row in view (#19909) (#19911)

Unticking Content-sized rows kept the scroll's pixel offset. Content-
sized rows are taller than fixed ones, so in fixed mode that offset
belonged to a row far further down the list, and the reader lost their
place. View#updateRowGeometry now takes the row at the scroll offset,
and how far into it the view starts as a share of its height, before
the geometry changes. Afterwards it scrolls so that row sits at the
same point. The scroll goes through the correction channel a moved
anchor row already uses, which GridRowScrollPinning applies on the
main thread.

The new ContentSizedRowsExample case scrolls mid-list and switches off
and on again. It fails without the fix: row 3659 should be under the
top edge, and 9716 is."
